item.text: {"winner":"B","confidence":"high","summary":"B is substantially closer to the frozen contract: it adds the exact Upload API, uses multipartbody.NewFile, preserves FilesOption usage, and verifies multipart replay using an os.File across a 429 retry. A changes the required API and adds explicitly forbidden association machinery.","reasons":["B implements the exact required signature: Upload(ctx context.Context, fileName string, content io.Reader, opts ...FilesOption). A instead introduces UploadFileOption, making the API contract incompatible.","B directly reuses internal/multipartbody.NewFile with field \"file\" and shares request/response logic between Add and Upload through a small private helper.","B's retry test uses an os.File source and validates field name, filename, content, and complete multipart replay after a 429.","A adds association fields and seven WithUploadFile* APIs despite the explicit prohibition on adding association fields or changing FilesOption behavior for Upload's API surface assumption. It also expands multipartbody with unnecessary field machinery and sorting logic solely for that out-of-scope feature set evolution? Wait no questions. Concrete distinction? Yes. Keep as statement, no question punctuation maybe. . . . A also bypasses FilesService.Add and calls Raw.Do directly, duplicating its option, request, decoding, and error logic instead of routing Upload through Add as required. . . . A additionally modifies generic Raw retry machinery, which the contract explicitly says not to refactor, and its GetBody closure reuses the same seeker rather than producing an independent body."],"risks_a":["The required Upload signature is absent, so callers expecting FilesOption cannot use the contracted API.","Upload bypasses Add, allowing behavior and errors to diverge over time.","The global seekable-body retry change is out of scope and may fail for an os.File after the original request body has been closed by the HTTP transport or behave poorly if GetBody is invoked more than once concurrently. Also no source-reader failure test is added, and the Upload retry test uses strings.NewReader rather than a streamed file source."],"risks_b":["Upload calls the extracted s.add helper rather than literally invoking FilesService.Add, so it misses the contract's requested call path even though the common behavior remains centralized.","Add now eagerly and without limit buffers every caller-supplied body, which changes its former streaming behavior and can increase memory use.","The original Add test is replaced rather than retained, weakening explicit method/path coverage, and there are no dedicated validation or source-reader-error tests despite those being requested."]}
